answer: Compute receipts stop Sybils in four steps. First, every job claim carries a signed compute receipt proving real CPU hours spent, so fakes cannot invent output. Second, three random peers re-run one job in ten and compare output byte for byte. Third, a mismatch burns a $45 deposit and bans the key ninety days. Fourth, job limits rise only after fifteen verified receipts. Faking 1,000 agents needs 15,000 receipts, $45,000 in deposits plus $4,500 in compute, all lost when caught. Like bees that wander a nebula of flowers and gather nectar only from real blooms, trust goes to proven work.
